pr_title: proxy/userspace: use waitgroups instead of sketchy atomic ops in testcases
pr_body:
Instead of relying on atomic ops to increment/decrement at the right time
just use waitgroups to provide hard synchronization points.

Supercedes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/93918

@liggitt @danwinship @kubernetes/sig-network-misc 

/kind cleanup
/kind failing-test
/kind flake

```release-note
NONE
```

Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/93904

@knight42 is that because something is not waiting for the previous stuff to be cleaned up, before trying to re-add the new endpoint?

issue_context.title: [sig-network] TestTCPProxyUpdateDeleteUpdate flakes with "error connecting to server" error
issue_context.body:
**Which test(s) are flaking**:

TestTCPProxyUpdateDeleteUpdate

**Reason for failure**:

```
E0811 20:46:12.851363 2432471 proxysocket.go:98] Couldn't find an endpoint for testnamespace/echo:p: missing endpoints
E0811 20:46:12.851726 2432471 proxysocket.go:144] Failed to connect to balancer: missing endpoints
--- FAIL: TestTCPProxyUpdateDeleteUpdate (0.06s)
    proxier_test.go:181: error connecting to server: Get "http://127.0.0.1:42275/aaaaa": http: server closed idle connection
FAIL
```

This is flaking rarely enough that it is not caught by our CI jobs, which currently tolerate up to 2 unit test failures per run (!).

With that toleration removed in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/93605, this flake has been seen (https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-jenkins/pr-logs/pull/93605/pull-kubernetes-bazel-test/1293275153643343872).

Reproducible with the following steps:

1. Build a test binary for the affected package:

```
go test -race -c ./pkg/proxy/userspace
```

2. Stress the affected test using the [stress](https://godoc.org/golang.org/x/tools/cmd/stress) tool:

```
stress ./userspace.test -test.run TestTCPProxyUpdateDeleteUpdate
```

5. Once failures are seen, look at the logs to see the details about the error:

```sh
ls -lat $TMPDIR/go-stress*
cat $TMPDIR/go-stress...<filename>
```

/sig network
cc @kubernetes/sig-network-test-failures
